scenario.prompt_to_agent:
A user on pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reports they lost all reach across the
data-center fabric -- pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) is unreachable, though pc_0_0
can still ping its own gateway 10.0.0.1. The NOC adds that both
spine routers reported their BGP session toward leaf_router_0_0 going
down at the same moment, while the leaf's uplink interfaces still
show UP. Diagnose.

injection.action: kill the BGP routing daemon (and watchfrr) on leaf_router_0_0

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: leaf_router_0_0 bgpd
Mechanism: leaf_router_0_0 is the top-of-rack leaf for pc_0_0
  (host subnet 10.0.0.0/24 on eth2). Its only fabric attachment is
  EBGP: neighbor 172.16.0.4 (spine_router_0_0, AS 65100) on eth0 and
  neighbor 172.16.0.8 (spine_router_0_1, AS 65101) on eth1. With bgpd
  dead the leaf stops learning 10.0.1.0/24 and stops advertising
  10.0.0.0/24, so pc_0_0 is isolated from the fabric even though every
  physical link is still UP.
Localization: leaf_router_0_0
Root cause: bgpd not running on leaf_router_0_0
Fix: restart FRR on leaf_router_0_0 (`service frr restart`) -- this lab
  keeps its config in /etc/frr/frr.conf, so a restart fully restores
  the BGP configuration and sessions.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03 on this fabric): bgpd is killed
together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh
remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO
`router bgp` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists bgpd. An agent
may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the bgp configuration is
missing/empty on leaf_router_0_0" -- that is the same fault observed at
the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
`service frr restart` on leaf_router_0_0. Unlike the vtysh-configured
kath labs, this lab has a persistent /etc/frr/frr.conf, so the restart
brings bgpd back WITH its full BGP configuration; the sessions to both
spines re-establish and pc_0_0 reaches pc_0_1 again.
scoring_axes: bonus-exonerates-fabric: notes the spines, the super-spine and leaf_router_0_1 are healthy (their other sessions stay Established), so the fault is only on leaf_router_0_0

agent.diagnosis_text:
The bgpd process on leaf_router_0_0 was forcibly killed (SIGKILL) at
05:06:42, and the watchfrr supervisor was also killed, preventing an
automatic restart. The FRR log ends with Zebra recording that its BGP
client (PID 58) disconnected and all BGP-installed routes were flushed
from the RIB — the characteristic footprint of an untrapped signal.
bgpd is absent from the process table, its PID file is a leftover
from the original start, and the running vtysh config is empty (only
zebra/staticd state remains). Because bgpd died, the TCP sessions to
both spine neighbors (172.16.0.4 on spine_router_0_0 and 172.16.0.8
on spine_router_0_1) were torn down simultaneously, which is exactly
what the NOC observed: both spines moved their 172.16.0.5 and
172.16.0.9 peer entries to Active state at the same instant. Without
those sessions, leaf_router_0_0 withdrew its advertisement of
10.0.0.0/24 and stopped receiving 10.0.1.0/24, leaving its RIB with
only directly-connected routes. pc_0_0 can still reach its gateway
(10.0.0.1 on eth2 of the leaf) because that is a local connected
route that zebra still holds, but any packet destined beyond the leaf
— in particular to pc_0_1's 10.0.1.0/24 subnet — is black-holed.

Root cause: bgpd was killed with SIGKILL on leaf_router_0_0, and
watchfrr was simultaneously killed so it could not restart the daemon.

Corrective fix: on leaf_router_0_0 run `systemctl restart frr` (or
`service frr restart`) to bring bgpd and watchfrr back up. FRR will
re-read /etc/frr/frr.conf, re-establish the two eBGP sessions to the
spines, exchange prefixes, and restore end-to-end reachability between
pc_0_0 and pc_0_1 within one BGP hold-time cycle (~90 s).

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names leaf_router_0_0 as the affected device in the diagnosis.
The report explicitly states bgpd on leaf_router_0_0 was killed and is absent from the process table, i.e., the BGP daemon is down.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-fabric: notes the spines, the super-spine and leaf_router_0_1 are healthy (their other sessions stay Established), so the fault is only on leaf_router_0_0
per_axis.rationale: The writeup describes bgpd death on leaf_router_0_0 and spine peer drops but does not state that the spines, super-spine, and leaf_router_0_1 (their other sessions) remained healthy/Established, so it fails to exonerate the fabric.
Recommends restarting the FRR service on leaf_router_0_0 (systemctl/service frr restart) to bring bgpd and watchfrr back up, matching the expected fix.

Minor uncertainty remains about the exact signal (SIGKILL) but the absence of shutdown logs and PID/process evidence makes that a reasonable inference.
